topic: Measurement of Inflation: WPI, CPI, and Indices
description: Inflation is the sustained increase in the general price level of goods and services in an economy over a period of time. In India, macroeconomic inflation is primarily measured and tracked using two key indices: the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) and the Consumer Price Index (CPI).

sections.title: Basic Concepts of Inflation Measurement
sections.description: Fundamental terminologies and conceptual frameworks used to calculate and analyze inflation rates.

key_concepts.explanation: A specific year serving as a reference point for comparing price changes over time. The index value for the base year is conventionally set to 100.
The measure of total inflation within an economy, including commodities such as food and energy prices, which tend to be highly volatile and experience sudden price spikes.
The underlying long-term trend of inflation calculated by excluding highly volatile items (like food and fuel) from the headline inflation figure.

sections.title: Wholesale Price Index (WPI)
sections.description: An indicator that measures and tracks the changes in the price of goods in the stages before the retail level.

key_concepts.explanation: It tracks the wholesale prices of a basket of goods traded between corporate entities and businesses, rather than goods bought by individual consumers.

key_associations.extra_info: Operates under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
WPI strictly measures goods and does not include services (like education, health, transport).
The WPI basket is heavily skewed towards Manufactured Products (64.23%), followed by Primary Articles (22.62%), and Fuel & Power (13.15%).

important_facts.fact: The current base year for calculating the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) in India is 2011-12.

sections.title: Consumer Price Index (CPI)
sections.description: A metric that examines the weighted average of prices of a basket of consumer goods and services, reflecting the actual cost of living.

key_concepts.explanation: It measures price changes from the perspective of a retail buyer. It acts as the primary indicator for measuring inflation affecting the common man.

key_associations.extra_info: Operates under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).
Unlike WPI, CPI includes price changes for services such as housing, education, medical care, and transportation.
Food and Beverages hold the highest weight in the CPI-Combined basket (approx. 45.86%), making CPI highly sensitive to food price shocks.

important_facts.fact: The current base year for CPI (Rural, Urban, and Combined) in India is 2012.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) officially adopted CPI-Combined as its key anchor measure for defining monetary policy and inflation targeting.

sections.title: Index of Industrial Production (IIP)
sections.description: A composite indicator that measures the short-term changes in the volume of production of a basket of industrial products.

key_concepts.explanation: It tracks manufacturing activity in different sectors of an economy. It compares industrial production in the current month against a reference base month/year.

key_associations.extra_info: IIP data is compiled and published monthly.
Comprises Coal, Crude Oil, Natural Gas, Refinery Products, Fertilizers, Steel, Cement, and Electricity. (Refinery products hold the highest individual weight).

important_facts.fact: The current base year for calculating the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is 2011-12.

sections.title: Inflation Targeting Framework
sections.description: The institutional and legislative mechanism established in India to maintain price stability while keeping in mind the objective of economic growth.

historical_events.significance: The committee recommended a shift from WPI to CPI as the primary nominal anchor for RBI's monetary policy and suggested a formal inflation targeting framework.

polity_articles.details: The RBI Act was amended in 2016 to provide a statutory basis for a flexible inflation targeting framework and the creation of a 6-member Monetary Policy Committee (MPC).

scientific_principles.application: The Central Government, in consultation with the RBI, set the inflation target at 4%, with an upper tolerance limit of 6% and a lower tolerance limit of 2%.
